La nouvelle cohorte de l’École Converse: The new École Converse cohort is thrilled to introduce Firas, Aya, Aude, Senan, Cindy and Sabrina, who for the past four weeks have been on a 12-week journey devoted to dialogue journalism. Together, they are learning to tell stories, to listen attentively and to give a voice to people who are often rendered invisible. Un immense merci à nos partenaires, qui: A huge thank you to our partners, who make this mission possible, and to everyone who follows École Converse and believes in it. We can't wait to show you their first stories! In the meantime, get to know them through portraits they wrote for one another.
De Tunis à Strasbourg, de Strasbourg à P: From Tunis to Strasbourg, from Strasbourg to Paris, from Paris back to Tunis, and finally landing in Montréal's sweltering July 2024 heat – that is the journey that brought Firas to École Converse. He has worked as a journalist for more than seven years, and at La Converse, he is filling a new page in his notebook.
Devant mon enregistreuse, Firas explique: In front of my recorder, Firas explains that the opportunity he has been given is a way of relearning a profession he has already known from other angles. “But what could an experienced journalist still have to learn?” I wondered. In fact, what he now wants to get used to is journalism “the Canadian way,” or rather “the Quebec way.”
« J’ai plutôt eu une carrière de journal: “I had more of a career as a journalist in Africa, where the job is tied to something a bit bigger; it's not such a neutral profession,” he says as he recounts his start in the field in Tunisia, a country ranked 118<sup>th</sup> in the <l1>World Press Freedom Index</l1>, published every year by Reporters Without Borders (RSF).
À Tunis, sa ville natale, il commence en: In Tunis, his hometown, he began by studying communication and politics. He got his first chance at a radio station, where he did press reviews. He then crossed the Mediterranean to Strasbourg to pursue studies in sociology. He later moved to Paris, where he covered sports news, his true passion.
Après quelques années, il remet les voil: After a few years, he set sail again and returned to Tunis, where he cut his teeth as a journalist. There, he went back to radio, covering sports on the most listened-to show in the country. He gained a certain reputation and joined the newsroom of Nawaat, a pioneering alternative media outlet focused on press freedom and respect for human rights.
De ce parcours atypique, Firas tire une: From this unconventional path, Firas draws a strength: a view of Canada shaped from abroad, which lets him observe his new host country through a singular lens.
À 22 ans à peine, Aya, une jeune Canadie: At barely 22, Aya, a young Canadian of Algerian origin who grew up in Montréal's east end, represents a generation ready to break the silence and open the world's eyes to realities that are too often ignored. A student in international relations and international law, she is driven by a deep desire to shine a light on the unseen and to remind us that everyone, regardless of origin, gender or history, deserves the same justice.
Son engagement prend vie au Forum Jeunes: Her commitment comes to life at the Forum Jeunesse de Saint-Michel, where she volunteers and co-hosts the podcast “Et si les jeunes avaient le pouvoir,” a platform where she tackles crucial issues affecting young people from visible minorities. From integration to intergenerational relationships, including the challenges specific to women, the podcast is a space where Aya helps amplify voices that are often marginalized. There, she explores gender inequality, structural barriers and everyday struggles, while sparking open discussions and looking for possible solutions.
Son parcours l’a menée à La Converse, un: Her path led her to La Converse, a media outlet that reflects values dear to her: equity, transparency and listening. For Aya, La Converse is not only a space for free expression, it is also a mirror held up to society to raise awareness, build bridges and inspire a dialogue that brings people together.
Dans tout ce qu’elle entreprend, Aya s’a: In everything she undertakes, Aya is committed to producing sincere stories that can make injustices resonate and inspire collective reflection. She doesn't just want to inform, but also to make people feel, to make them understand and to make them act. Her writing, full of humanity and transparency, is a call to open our eyes to what we sometimes prefer not to see.
Laissez-vous interpeller par le regard i: Let yourself be challenged by Aya's incisive gaze and discover with her stories that deserve to be heard.
C’est dans les rues animées de Montréal-: It was in the lively streets of Montréal-Nord and Rivière-des-Prairies that Sabrina, a 24-year-old woman, forged the unique perspective she brings to the city's social dynamics. Of Algerian origin and raised in these neighbourhoods, she witnessed the challenges visible minorities face and saw the complex mechanisms that shape their daily lives.
Elle est peut-être arrivée par hasard à: She may have arrived at École Converse by chance, but for Sabrina it now feels obvious: this outlet has become the space where she can bring her ideas to life, exploring with nuance and authenticity realities that are often overlooked. A graduate in political communication, Sabrina stands out for her ability to decode social issues and offer thoughtful, accessible perspectives on them.
Pour elle, écrire ne se limite pas à la: For her, writing isn't limited to conveying emotions or facts. It is an act of connection and a way of linking individual stories to collective issues, while offering keys to understanding. In her writing, Sabrina doesn't simply seek to inform, but also to inspire constructive dialogue and provoke reflection that resonates beyond words.
Son approche rigoureuse et sensible l’am: Her rigorous yet sensitive approach leads her to create stories that challenge and awaken consciences. With a pen that is both factual and deeply human, she sheds light on realities that deserve to be recognized and understood. Sabrina is an analytical pen in the service of a more aware society.
Sènan débarque à l’École Converse pour é: Sènan arrives at École Converse to write a new story. Her own. Originally from Gatineau, she grew up with the background noise of the evening news, a constant presence in the family home. That sound guided her to the university lecture halls, where she studied journalism in Montréal in 2019.
Un stylo dans une main, un ballon orange: A pen in one hand, an orange basketball – her other passion – in the other, Sènan juggles images and words with a clear goal: to practise journalism rooted in the reality of the people whose stories she tells.
Sa première expérience dans le journalis: Her first experience in journalism is energetic. After graduating in 2023, she nonetheless faced headwinds in breaking into a newsroom and went through personal trials. A timeout became necessary, a needed retreat to catch her breath. The pause allowed her to recharge so she could start again stronger. Today, she is back with renewed determination.
L’École Converse est son point de relanc: École Converse is her relaunch point, a space where she hopes to refine her craft of journalism, resilient and humanist, in tune with the voices of the most vulnerable. She champions journalism that is visual, captivating and brings dialogue with it, journalism that touches and connects.
Sènan, un « n » muet à la fin mais une v: Sènan, with a silent “n” at the end but an unmistakable will, places kindness at the heart of her approach. Tall and ambitious, she is a journalist in the making, ready to write a more human, more just story.
Cindy Lufuluabo est étudiante à la maîtr: Cindy Lufuluabo is a master's student in public health. Her years of research experience and her interest in community connection fuel her desire for justice and knowledge.
« <em>Knowledge is power</em> », cite-t-: “Knowledge is power,” she says with a smile as she talks about what brought her to La Converse.
Originaire du Congo et ayant grandi à Sa: Originally from Congo and raised in Saint-Laurent, she says she has too often seen people address marginalized communities without any empathy. She firmly believes these communities hold the key to their own liberation, in their own stories. For her, it is essential to have a moment of genuine exchange in order to truly understand others.
Avec sa riche connaissance du milieu de: With her deep knowledge of the research world, Cindy thrives in the art of human exploration. Her avid curiosity about life stories and individual journeys has led her down a path where every encounter becomes an opportunity to better discover the richness and complexity of personal experience.
Son regard bienveillant révèle cependant: Her caring gaze reveals, however, that her commitment doesn't stop there. Convinced that access to knowledge should not be reserved for an elite, she seeks to reveal truths that are often rendered invisible. For Cindy, it is essential to make ideas and information accessible to everyone and to fight the barriers that keep some people from learning and emancipating themselves.
Avec son implication à La Converse, elle: Through her involvement at La Converse, she says she is pursuing three goals: to forge connections, to deepen human connection and to break down age-old barriers.
Fille d’immigrants haïtiens, Aude Simon,: The daughter of Haitian immigrants, Aude Simon, 27, grew up on Montréal's South Shore. Passionate about capturing the stories of those whose stories are too rarely told, she is driven by a deep desire to make often ignored voices heard. She holds a bachelor's degree in film studies and has long dreamed of making a documentary. For her, video is a unique medium, able to portray life with unmatched depth, capturing the nonverbal, the smiles and the glances – all elements that transcend words.
C’est son amour pour la vidéo qui lui a: It was her love of video that led her to discover journalism, a path that allows her to regularly produce content while bringing her closer to her ultimate goal. After working with various media outlets, Aude was drawn to La Converse, which she saw as a different kind of space, in tune with her values.
En tant que personne vivant à l’intersec: As someone living at the intersection of several identities, Aude joined La Converse to work in an environment where diversity is celebrated. She sees it as an opportunity to give a platform to Black, immigrant and queer communities, whose voices are often overlooked by traditional media.
Au-delà de l’acquisition de compétences: Beyond acquiring journalistic skills, Aude sees École Converse as a space where she can draw on her own lived experience to connect with others and cultivate ever greater empathy.
